title: Signature Importance-Weighted Allocation — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Not all searches matter equally, so the budget manager splits the total budget — seconds, API calls, compute — across active searches in proportion to their importance weights. A user's interactive query outranks a background crawl; a legal audit outranks a casual browse. Weights are set by policy with per-mission overrides, and the allocation is recomputed whenever missions start or finish. Explicit allocation replaces hope with arithmetic in resource contention. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Expected-Value Cutoff — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Every additional unit of search buys diminishing expected information, and the cutoff rule stops spending when the marginal expected value drops below the marginal cost. Expected value is estimated from the mission's progress curve — how fast useful results have been arriving. This is the rational core of 'good enough': keep going while it pays, stop when it does not. Cutoffs make the budget manager principled rather than merely thrifty. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Time-Box Enforcement — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. A time box is a hard deadline per search phase: the manager starts a timer, and when it fires the phase returns whatever it has, marked partial. Enforcement is non-negotiable — a runaway deep search cannot eat the budget meant for five other missions. Partial results carry a completeness estimate so consumers know what they are getting. Time boxes turn 'search until done' into 'search until useful or until time', which is the only schedule that survives contact with boundless archives. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
import time
def boxed_search(seconds):
    end = time.time() + seconds
    out, i = [], 0
    while time.time() < end:
        out.append("r%d" % i); i += 1
    return out, False
res, complete = boxed_search(0.05)
print("returned %d results, complete=%s" % (len(res), complete))

title: Signature Mid-Search Reallocation — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Budgets set at the start are guesses, so the manager re-evaluates mid-search: missions beating expectations earn more budget, stalled ones get cut. Reallocation runs on a schedule — every N seconds or every M results — using the same importance weights plus observed progress. Freed budget flows to the highest marginal value, never back to a global pool to sit idle. Adaptive reallocation is what makes the budget manager adaptive rather than just a planner. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Utility Tracking — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. To allocate well tomorrow, the manager tracks utility today: results per unit budget, per mission class, per strategy. Utility histories reveal which strategies pay off — deep federation versus quick indexes — and feed the next allocation cycle. Tracking is lightweight counters, not heavy instrumentation, so it never costs more than it saves. A budget manager that learns from its own spending gets smarter every mission. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
